text:
Alex (Support): Hey team — ACME reported their Dedicated pool drained most of the reserved GPU hours overnight even though their token usage was steady. Customer says they didn't change traffic patterns. Can someone take a look?

Maya (Billing): Acknowledge, opening an invoice/usage pull. Do we have the dedicated pool id and the time window?

Alex (Support): Pool id: ded-az1-acme-42. Window: 2026-03-01 00:00 -> 2026-03-02 06:00 UTC. They show baseline ~120k tokens/hour but GPU-hours spiked from 5h->38h in that window. No obvious error in their app logs.

Zheng (Platform): I'll check autoscale & burst settings. Quick Q: are we sure "reserved_gpu_hours" meter is the one increasing, not the "burst_gpu_hours" or a fallback mapping?

billing-bot: [system] Applied burst credits to customer acme-inc (ded-az1-acme-42) at 2026-03-01T03:12:09Z — meter: reserved_gpu_hours delta:+32.0h reason: emergency-burst-fallback

Alex (Support): That's odd — why would burst credits increment reserved hours? Customer didn't request emergency burst. They only reported 502 retries earlier at 03:10 UTC then traffic was fine.

Rob (SRE): Possible explanation: when capacity in Dedicated pool is exhausted we route to higher-tier fallback that maps to the same billing meter incorrectly. Need to check routing policy for that pool and the meter mapping table. I'll pull routing logs.

Zheng (Platform): Reproduced in staging: if the autoscaler hits "max_pool_replicas" it flips to fallback routing which incorrectly uses the reserved meter id. Patch idea: ensure fallback routes set meter_id="burst_gpu_hours".

Maya (Billing): For reconciliation we need three pieces: 1) time series of pool replica counts, 2) routing decisions log, 3) billing events for that customer. Alex, can you get customer request ids around 03:09-03:15?

Alex (Support): Provided below (redacted): request ids: [r-9a1, r-9a2, r-9a7]. Customer logs show repeated 502s then rapid retry loop from their side.

Zheng (Platform): I dumped the router trace for ded-az1-acme-42 — snippet: 
```
2026-03-01T03:11:52Z ROUTER route_request customer=acme-inc pool=ded-az1-acme-42 status=overloaded -> fallback_pool=ded-fallback-std
2026-03-01T03:12:03Z BILLING emit_event customer=acme-inc meter_id=reserved_gpu_hours value=16.0h source=router
2026-03-01T03:12:09Z BILLING apply_credit customer=acme-inc type=burst
```
Zheng (Platform): So router emitted billing events with meter_id=reserved_gpu_hours when it routed to fallback. That's our bug.

Maya (Billing): That would cause dashboard vs invoice mismatch: monitoring dashboards query meter "burst_gpu_hours" for burst activity, but invoices aggregated reserved_gpu_hours. We need to correct meter_id mapping and run a backfill.

Sara (Product): How big is the customer impact? If we backfill, do we issue credit? What's the policy?

Maya (Billing): Preliminary: customer billed for +32h on reserved hours which is wrong. We'll prepare a credit equal to those hours at their reserved rate. I'll draft a credit memos and mark ticket escalated.

Rob (SRE): Quick reproducible steps for platform team (staging):
1) Create Dedicated pool with max_replicas=2 and a fallback pool configured.
2) Send a tight retry loop to overwhelm replicas (curl loop with concurrency).
3) Observe router emits billing event with meter_id=reserved_gpu_hours.
4) Confirm that changing router fallback config to meter_id=burst_gpu_hours fixes emitted events.

Example commands we used: 
```
# hammer the endpoint
for i in {1..400}; do curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/complete -H "Authorization: Bearer stg-..." -d '{"model":"redwood-ded-42","input":"test"}' & done
# check router trace
curl -s "https://staging-internal/routers/trace?pool=ded-az1-acme-42&from=2026-03-01T03:00:00Z&to=2026-03-01T03:30:00Z" | jq .
```

Zheng (Platform): I'll patch router to use explicit meter mapping and deploy to prod canary. Rob can validate in prod canary window.

Alex (Support): Communicated to customer: "we've found an internal routing -> billing mapping issue that caused reserved GPU hours to be recorded for fallback burst events. We're preparing a credit and a fix; will follow up with timeline." They asked for ETA.

Maya (Billing): ETA: patch to router mapping in ~2 business hours, backfill script in ~1 day, credit issued within 48 hours after validation. I'll CC account team.

Rob (SRE): After patch we'll also add an alert: if reserved_gpu_hours delta >= 10h within 30m AND token rate did not increase >50% then page on-call. Prevent silent billing spikes.

Sara (Product): Also add a dashboard view comparing meter_id counts side-by-side for last 7 days so customers can spot anomalies.

Alex (Support): Thanks all — closing loop with customer now. Will paste AP ticket once credit is issued. :thumbsup:

Maya (Billing): Filing follow-up: billing ticket #BILL-1789 for ACME credit.

billing-bot: [system] Credit issued to account acme-inc amount=$1920 (32h @ $60/h) memoid=BILL-1789 timestamp=2026-03-02T14:04:00Z

Alex (Support): Customer replied: "Thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround." Thread resolved."
